_what_this_is: The commitment-discount rates the Optimized cost TIER applies, shared by every migration skill so the tier means the same thing in every report. Optimized = Balanced with these rates applied ONLY to the RI/SP-eligible subtotal (eligibility per ri-sp-eligibility.md in this same shared/estimate directory); the ineligible subtotal is unchanged. These are TIER rates, not the post-migration opportunity ranges: a skill's optimization_opportunities[] rows quote the wider all-term ranges (e.g. 20-66%) from its own estimate-defaults.json.
midpoint_rule: Each rate below is the arithmetic mid-point of the typical 1-year, no-upfront range for that commitment product (compute_savings_plan), or the stated maximum where AWS publishes only an 'up to' figure for the product (database_savings_plan_provisioned: AWS states up to 20% on provisioned instances). Where AWS publishes a LOWER maximum for one service, that service uses its cap from service_caps instead: apply min(product rate, service cap). Apply the rate to the eligible line's Balanced on-demand amount, round each line's discount to whole dollars, sum, and record the rate(s) and both subtotals in the estimate artifact (projected_costs._optimized_basis).
eligibility_source: ri-sp-eligibility.md (this directory; vendored into each skill at references/vendored/estimate/ri-sp-eligibility.md). A service with no eligible row there is ineligible and its line is unchanged.

applies_to: EC2 (including the EC2 component of Elastic Beanstalk and EKS nodes)
compute_savings_plan.source: AWS Compute Savings Plans: up to 66% at the maximum term; the typical 1-year no-upfront saving is 20-40% (the figure the gcp-to-aws Part 3 commitment table and the azure-to-aws Optimized basis already use).

database_savings_plan_provisioned.source: AWS Database Savings Plans: up to 20% on provisioned engines (up to 35% on serverless, which is not a tier input because the tier prices the designed capacity).

service_caps._rule: AWS publishes a lower maximum for these services than the product rate above, so the tier applies the cap, never the product rate: rate_applied = min(product rate, cap). A service with no entry here uses its product rate.

aws_lambda.applies_to_charge: duration (on-demand and provisioned concurrency) and provisioned-concurrency charges; not Lambda requests
aws_lambda.source: AWS News Blog, 'Savings Plan Update - Save up to 17% on your Lambda workloads' (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/savings-plan-update-save-up-to-17-on-your-lambda-workloads/), read 2026-11-26.

dynamodb_and_keyspaces_on_demand_through.source: AWS News Blog, 'Introducing Database Savings Plans for AWS Databases' (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/introducing-database-savings-plans-for-aws-databases/), read 2026-11-26: DynamoDB and Keyspaces on-demand throughput up to 18%.

dynamodb_and_keyspaces_provisioned_capac.source: AWS News Blog, 'Introducing Database Savings Plans for AWS Databases' (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/introducing-database-savings-plans-for-aws-databases/), read 2026-11-26: DynamoDB and Keyspaces provisioned capacity up to 12%.

not_tier_inputs: Spot pricing, S3 Intelligent-Tiering / Infrequent Access, Reserved Instances with upfront payment, ElastiCache Reserved Nodes, Graviton re-platforming, and every other consumption-model, storage-class or architecture assumption. Those are optimization_opportunities[] rows with their own savings ranges.
when_tiers_coincide: If no priced line is eligible, Optimized equals Balanced and the report must say so where the reader sees the equal figures (report-decision-core.md, How to read the tiers).
